sentences.text: The prosecution case, in brief, is that on 21.08.2021, the deceased Smt. Kranti Ahirwar died allegedly due to an epileptic attack.
On 17.09.2021, her husband Dhaniram Ahirwar lodged a report stating that his wife died due to epilepsy.
On the basis of this report, Chandrashekhar Pandey (PW-12) registered Marg No. 23/2021 (Ex.P-21) at Police Station Dharampur.
The police prepared a spot map (Ex.P-3).
During the Marg inquiry, the inquest proceedings (Shav Panchanama) were conducted by Dhirendra Kumar Gautam, Naib Tehsildar (PW-8), and Naksha Panchayatnama was prepared.

Thereafter, the dead body of the deceased was sent for post-mortem examination to the Community Health Centre, Ajaygarh, where the post- mortem report (Ex.P-12) was prepared by Dr.
Vipin Patel (PW-10).

Indrapal Ahirwar (PW-14) brought the viscera of the deceased--heart, liver,
lungs, spleen, kidneys, stomach, and intestines--from CHC Ajaygarh in sealed containers, which were seized at Police Station Dharampur vide seizure memo Ex.P-22.
Subsequently, the dead body was handed over to the family members through Ex.P-24.
Statements of witnesses were recorded during the investigation.
During inquiry, the deceased's father Kamlesh stated that Kranti was married to Dhaniram on 29.04.2016 as per Hindu customs and that dowry articles were given as per his financial capacity.
He stated that his second daughter Bharti was married in the year 2020, and at that time, Dhaniram and his mother Rajjibai were present.
He alleged that after Bharti's marriage, Dhaniram and Rajjibai started harassing Kranti for bringing one lakh rupees and household articles such as a bed and cooler.
Due to non- fulfilment of the dowry demand, Kranti was allegedly beaten and subjected to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:15864 3 CRA-7677-2023 physical and mental cruelty.
It was further alleged that on 18.08.2021, the deceased called her sister Shivkumari and stated that Dhaniram had beaten and strangled her, due to which she was unable to speak properly.

On the basis of these allegations, FIR (Ex.P-13) was registered by B.S. Parihar (PW- 11) against accused Dhaniram and Rajjibai under Sections 498-A, 304-B, 34 IPC and Sections 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
The marriage card of the deceased was seized as Ex.P-1.
Accused Rajjibai and Dhaniram were arrested on 12.01.2022 and 21.02.2022 respectively.

6. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the appellant/State submitted that the learned Trial Court has arbitrarily acquitted the accused persons without properly appreciating the evidence on record.

It was argued that the Trial Court committed a grave error in law by ignoring material evidence showing that the deceased committed suicide due to continuous cruelty and harassment by the accused on account of dowry demand.

The Trial Court allegedly failed to properly rely upon the testimonies of the deceased's sister (PW-1), father (PW-2), brother (PW-5), aunt (PW-6), and uncle (PW-9), who supported the prosecution case regarding cruelty and dowry-related harassment.

It is further submitted that minor discrepancies in witness testimonies should have been ignored in view of the settled legal principle laid down in Saiyad Ahmad v. State of Karnataka, 2012 (3) Crime 2020 (SC).

He also admitted in his cross-examination that the people present at the scene did not mention anything about the assault over dowry.

Dr. Vipin Patel (PW-10) deposed that on 22.08.2021 he was posted as Medical Officer at the Community Health Center, Ajaygarh and he NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:15864 11 CRA-7677-2023 conducted autopsy of deceased and opined that the death of the deceased Kranti appeared to have occurred within 36 hours of the examination due to cardiac and respiratory arrest.

sentences.text: B.S. Parihar (PW-11) stated that on 17.09.2021, he was posted as Sub-Divisional Officer of Police in the Ajaygarh Sub-Division.

He stated that on said date, he investigated Marg No. 23/2021 at Dharampur Police Station and after completion of investigation, a First Information Report was registered against the accused Dhaniram Ahirwar and Mrs. Rajji Bai under sections 498A, 304B, 34 of the Indian Penal Code and 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
The First Information Report is Exhibit P-13.

During the investigation, the statements of Baldau Ahirwar, Satendra Ahirwar,
Shivkumari Ahirwar, Kamlesh Ahirwar, Desrani Ahirwar on 18.09.2021, witness Sambhu Prasad Ahirwar on 21.09.2021 and Rammilan Lodh on 27.09.2021 were recorded by him as per their version.
He had sent the seized articles for forensic examination to Forensic Laboratory, Sagar through the Superintendent of Police, Panna, District Panna.
The receipt of FSL Sagar is Ex.P-15.
He also stated that he arrested the accused Dhaniram and Rajji Bai.

21. The investigating officers (PW-11 and PW-12) confirmed that initial Marg proceedings were conducted on the information given by the accused and that no allegation of assault or dowry harassment was made at that time.

22. After carefully considering the submissions advanced by the learned Government Advocate and upon a thorough reappraisal of the evidence available on record, this Court is of the considered opinion that no interference is warranted with the judgment of acquittal passed by the learned Trial Court.

23. In the present case, the prosecution has failed to establish the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:15864 13 CRA-7677-2023 essential ingredients of the offences under Sections 498-A and 304-B of the Indian Penal Code beyond reasonable doubt.

Though allegations of dowry demand and cruelty were made by the relatives of the deceased, it is evident from their own admissions in cross-examination that no complaint or report regarding such alleged harassment was ever lodged during the subsistence of the marriage, which lasted for nearly four years.
The evidence further reveals that the deceased was suffering from epilepsy even prior to her marriage and had been hospitalized several times for treatment.

The medical evidence, particularly the testimony of Dr. Vipin Patel (PW-10), clearly rules out death by strangulation or physical assault, as no ligature marks or external injuries suggestive of violence were found on the body of the deceased.
The injuries noted during post-mortem, including the tongue bite and abrasions are consistent with an epileptic attack.
Significantly, the initial Marg inquiry, inquest proceedings, and spot panchnama do not disclose any allegation of dowry related cruelty or assault.
The allegations surfaced only after a considerable delay, which further weakens the prosecution case.
Moreover, none of the independent witnesses supported the allegation of dowry demand or harassment.

24. To attract the presumption under Section 113-B of the Indian Evidence Act, the prosecution is required to prove that the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment "soon before her death"
in connection with demand for dowry.
In the present case, the prosecution has failed to establish this crucial link.

Mere general and omnibus allegations, without contemporaneous corroboration,
are insufficient to sustain a conviction under Section 304-B IPC.

The learned Trial Court has meticulously analyzed the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:15864 14 CRA-7677-2023 oral and documentary evidence and has assigned cogent and convincing reasons for acquitting the The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Dhaniram Ahirwar on 24 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104925192/
7 accused persons.

25. Accordingly, this criminal appeal is dismissed and the judgment of acquittal dated 28.02.2023 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Panna, in S.T. No. 46/2022 is affirmed.
26. Record of the trial Court be sent back immediately.

After carefully considering the submissions advanced by the learned Government Advocate and upon a thorough reappraisal of the evidence available on record, this Court is of the considered opinion that no interference is warranted with the judgment of acquittal passed by the learned Trial Court.
23. In the present case, the prosecution has failed to establish the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

Though allegations of dowry demand and cruelty were made by the relatives of the deceased, it is evident from their own admissions in cross-examination that no complaint or report regarding such alleged harassment was ever lodged during the subsistence of the marriage, which lasted for nearly four years.
The evidence further reveals that the deceased was suffering from epilepsy even prior to her marriage and had been hospitalized several times for treatment.
The medical evidence, particularly the testimony of Dr. Vipin Patel (PW-10), clearly rules out death by strangulation or physical assault, as no ligature marks or external injuries suggestive of violence were found on the body of the deceased.
The injuries noted during post-mortem, including the tongue bite and abrasions are consistent with an epileptic attack.
Significantly, the initial Marg inquiry, inquest proceedings, and spot panchnama do not disclose any allegation of dowry related cruelty or assault.
The allegations surfaced only after a considerable delay, which further weakens the prosecution case.
Moreover, none of the independent witnesses supported the allegation of dowry demand or harassment.
24. To attract the presumption under Section 113-B of the Indian Evidence Act, the prosecution is required to prove that the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment "soon before her death"
in connection with demand for dowry.
In the present case, the prosecution has failed to establish this crucial link.
Mere general and omnibus allegations, without contemporaneous corroboration,
are insufficient to sustain a conviction under Section 304-B IPC.
